reasoning: Combined the overlapping coverage, outcome-mapping, and final-audit guidance into one edit. Merged the two flat-list serialization proposals, while retaining the distinct guidance on unrequested optional parameters and unavailable operations. Support counts reflect how many of the four source patches support each consolidated edit. [optimizer-ranked: selected 3/4 edits]

edits.target: - Turn each explicit clause into a requested action, target, and set of qualifiers. In one-turn tasks, narrated sequences such as “first,” “then,” and “finally” describe requested actions, not actions already completed.
edits.content: - A clause may request multiple outcomes: split coordinated operations or deliverables joined by “and,” “also,” or equivalent wording into separate action–target–qualifier sets unless one endpoint explicitly provides them together. Distinguish separate sources or platforms and separate operations on the same target. Keep identifiers, sources, filters, and dates bound to their own outcome. In the final coverage audit, scan the request from its last clause backward and match every outcome to a call that satisfies its specific result and scope; a related call does not cover a distinct outcome.

edits.target: - Distinguish parameters that can be confused, such as quantities versus repetitions or operation-specific values versus ordinary search terms. Include supported optional parameters needed to express explicit constraints; do not silently relax a constrained request. Use documented defaults only when they fit the request, and do not invent unsupported arguments, identifiers, credentials, or values.
edits.content: - Do not add a supported optional parameter unless it expresses a user-requested qualifier. Do not infer units, locale, sorting, or filters from context; use the endpoint’s documented default when no such qualifier was requested.

edits.target: - Choose an endpoint by its documented operation, output, target, and support for the requested qualifiers—not merely by a shared topic or entity name. Prefer the most specific endpoint that fits the request; use separate endpoints when distinct deliverables require them.
edits.content: - If the requested operation is unavailable, do not invent a tool or substitute a merely related operation. Use an available endpoint only when its documented output satisfies the requested result and scope; otherwise, do not present a different result as coverage.

ranking_details.reasoning: Edit 0 most directly prevents missed deliverables and qualifier mix-ups across multi-part requests. Edit 2 adds a general safeguard against inferring unrequested parameters, complementing the existing schema guidance. Edit 1 clarifies what to do when no endpoint fits, though endpoint selection guidance already covers much of its concern. Edit 3 largely repeats the existing answer-structure rules.
